The high court refused to intervene in a case involving 20,000 people the Republican administration flagged as likely noncitizens on the largely Democratic state's voter rolls.
It was the latest in a flurry of election-related litigation the day before the midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress for the last two years of Trump's second term.
In California, the Trump administration had asked the high court to set aside the challenged ballots until the voters' citizenship status could be verified. The high court did not detail its reasoning, as is common in emergency decisions.

articles.title: SC says 'don't travel by air', refuses urgent hearing on airfare hike plea
articles.summary:
Don't travel by air, the Supreme Court told a petitioner on Monday while refusing urgent listing of a plea alleging nearly 700 per cent increase in airfares.
An advocate mentioned the matter for urgent listing before a bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Aparesh Kumar Singh.
"The aviation fare has increased by 700 per cent," the advocate said.
"Don't travel by air," the bench observed.
The advocate then said air travel is an essential service. "It's a violation of Article 14."
Article 14 of the Constitution deals with equality before law.
